sanskrit: diśaś catasro 'śvataryo devarathasya puroḍāśāḥ śaphā antarikṣam uddhiḥ ||
english: The four directions are the mule-mares of the divine chariot; the oblation-portions are its hooves; the atmosphere is its upward shaft.

sanskrit: dyāvāpṛthivī pakṣasī ṛtavo 'bhīśavo vāk parirathyam ||
english: Heaven and earth are its two wings; the seasons are the reins; speech is the outer road of the chariot.

sanskrit: ahorātre cakre māsā arāḥ saṃvatsaro adhiṣṭhānam ||
english: Day and night are the two wheels; the months are the spokes; the year is the axle-base.

sanskrit: virāḍ īṣāgnī rathamukham indraḥ savyaṣṭhāś candramāḥ sārathiḥ ||
english: Virāj is the pole; the two fires are the front of the chariot; Indra is the left-standing one; the Moon is the charioteer.

sanskrit: ito jayeto vi jayasva jaya saṃ jaya svāhā ||
english: From here conquer, conquer thoroughly, conquer, conquer altogether — svāhā!

sanskrit: divas pṛthivyā antarikṣāt samudrād agner vātān madhukaśā hi jajñe | tāṃ cāyitvāmṛtaṃ vasānāṃ hṛdbhiḥ prajāḥ prati nandanti sarvāḥ ||
english: For Madhukaśā was born from heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere, from the ocean, from fire, from the winds. Having waited upon her, all creatures clad in immortality rejoice with their hearts.

sanskrit: paśyanty asyāś caritaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pṛthaṅ naro bahudhā mīmāṃsamānāḥ | agner vātān madhukaśā hi jajñe marutām ugrā naptiḥ ||
english: Men behold her movement upon the earth, severally, pondering her in many ways. For Madhukaśā was born from fire and the winds — the fierce granddaughter of the Maruts.

sanskrit: mahad viśvarūpaṃ payo asyāḥ samudrasyota tvā reta āhuḥ | yata aiti madhukaśā rarāṇā tat prāṇas tad amṛtaṃ niviṣṭam ||
english: Great and all-formed is her milk; they call it the seed of the ocean. Whence Madhukaśā comes forth rejoicing — there is the breath of life, there immortality is lodged.

sanskrit: mātādityānāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ prāṇaḥ prajānām amṛtasya nābhiḥ | hiraṇyavarṇā madhukaśā ghṛtācī mahad bhargaś carati martyeṣu ||
english: Mother of the Ādityas, daughter of the Vasus, the breath of creatures, the navel of immortality — golden-hued Madhukaśā, radiant with ghee, moves as a great splendour among mortals.

sanskrit: madhoḥ kaśām ajanayanta devās tasyā garbho abhavad viśvarūpam | taṃ jātaṃ taruṇaṃ piparti mātā sa jāto viśvā bhuvanābhi vaste ||
english: The gods gave birth to the whip of honey; her womb became all-formed. The mother nourishes him newly born and tender; he, once born, clothes all the worlds.

sanskrit: kas tau pra veda ka u tau na āha yāv asyā stanau sahasradhārāv akṣitau | ūrjaṃ duhāte anapasphurantau ||
english: Who truly knows them? Who has declared them — her two breasts that flow in a thousand streams, imperishable, milking out vigour without ever shrinking?

sanskrit: kas taṃ pra veda ka u taṃ ciketa yo asyā hṛdaḥ kalaśaḥ somadhāno akṣitaḥ | brahmā sumedhāḥ so asmin madeta ||
english: Who truly knows it? Who has discerned it — that vessel of her heart, the imperishable Soma-receptacle? May a brahman of sound understanding rejoice therein.

sanskrit: hiṅkarikratī bṛhatī vayodhā uccairghoṣābhi yāti yā vratā | trīn gharmān abhi vāvaśānā mimāti māyuṃ payate payobhiḥ ||
english: She who moves to the rites with the hiṅkāra-call — great, sustaining life, resounding loudly — lowing repeatedly toward the three ritual heatings, she bellows her cry, she yields milk with her streams.

sanskrit: yām āpīnām upa sīdanty āpo yāṃ śakvarā vṛṣabhā yāṃ svarājaḥ | te varṣanti te varṣayanti tad vide kāmam ūrjam āpaḥ ||
english: The waters approach her as she is full-uddered; the mighty bulls approach her; the self-rulers approach her. They rain, they cause it to rain — in that the waters know desire and nourishment.

sanskrit: stanayitnus te vāk prajāpate vṛṣā śuṣmaṃ kṣipasi bhūmyām adhi | agner vātān madhukaśā hi jajñe marutām ugrā naptiḥ ||
english: Your thunder is your voice, O Prajāpati; as bull you cast your vigour down upon the earth. For Madhukaśā was born from fire and the winds — the fierce granddaughter of the Maruts.

sanskrit: yathā somaḥ prātaḥsavane aśvinor bhavati priyaḥ | evā me aśvinā varca ātmani dhriyatām ||
english: As Soma at the morning pressing becomes dear to the Aśvins, even so let the Aśvins hold radiant lustre within my self.

sanskrit: yathā somo dvitīyasavana indrāgnyor bhavati priyaḥ | evā ma indrāgnī varcaḥ (…) ||
english: As Soma at the midday pressing becomes dear to Indra and Agni, even so let Indra and Agni hold lustre [within my self].

sanskrit: yathā somas tṛtīyasavana ṛbhūṇāṃ bhavati priyaḥ | evā ma ṛbhavo varca ātmani dhriyatām ||
english: As Soma at the third pressing becomes dear to the Ṛbhus, even so let the Ṛbhus hold radiant lustre within my self.

sanskrit: madhu janiṣīya madhu maṃsiṣīya | payasvān agna āgamaṃ taṃ mā saṃ sṛja varcasā ||
english: May I be born in honey, may I think in honey. I have come to you, O Agni, rich in milk — unite me with lustre.

sanskrit: saṃ māgne varcasā sṛja saṃ prajayā sam āyuṣā | vidyur me asya devā indro vidyāt saha ṛṣibhiḥ ||
english: Unite me, O Agni, with lustre; unite me with offspring; unite me with long life. May the gods know this of me; may Indra know it together with the seers.

sanskrit: yad giriṣv iti pāñcarcikī ||
english: [Colophon:] "That which is on the mountains" — this is a five-verse sūkta.

sanskrit: yathā madhu madhukṛtaḥ saṃbharanti madhāv adhi | evā me aśvinā balam ojaś ca dhriyatām ||
english: As the honey-makers gather honey upon honey, even so let the Aśvins hold strength and vital force within me.

sanskrit: yathā makṣā idaṃ madhu nyañjanti kṣaṇāv adhi | evā me aśvinā varcas tejaś ca dhriyatām ||
english: As bees smear this honey upon the honeycomb, even so let the Aśvins hold lustre and blazing energy within me.

sanskrit: aśvinā sāragheṇa mā madhunāṅktaṃ śubhaspatī | yathā varcasvatīṃ vācam ā vadāni janām̐ anu ||
english: O Aśvins, lords of auspiciousness, anoint me with the honey of the bee, so that I may speak lustrous speech among the people.

sanskrit: vṛṣā śuṣmaṃ kṣipasi bhūmyāṃ divo madhoḥ kaśayā pṛthivīm anakṣi | tāṃ jātāṃ paśava upa jīvanti sarve teno seṣam ūrjaṃ piparti ||
english: As bull you cast vigour upon the earth; with the honey-whip from heaven you have anointed the earth. All creatures live by her once she is born; therewith does she nourish the remaining vigour.
